passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Consolidated Results of Operations and Financial Condition Overview We are a global market leader in the design, development, manufacture, sale, service and support of commercial jetliners, military aircraft, satellites, missile defense, human space flight and launch systems and services. We are one of the two major manufacturers of 100+ seat airplanes for the worldwide commercial airline industry and one of the largest defense contractors in the U.S. While our principal operations are in the U.S., we conduct operations in an expanding number of countries and rely on an extensive network of U.S. and non-U.S. partners, key suppliers and subcontractors. Our strategy is centered on successful execution in healthy core businesses – Commercial Airplanes (BCA), Defense, Space & Security (BDS) and Global Services (BGS). BCA is committed to offering airplanes that deliver superior design, safety, quality, efficiency and value to customers around the world. BDS integrates its resources in defense, intelligence, communications, security, space and services to deliver capability-driven solutions to customers. Our BDS strategy is to leverage our core businesses to capture key next-generation programs while expanding our presence in adjacent and international markets. BGS provides support for commercial and defense customers through innovative, comprehensive and cost-competitive product and service solutions. On January 5, 2024, a 737-9 flight made an emergency landing after a mid-exit door plug detached in flight. As a result of the accident, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) performed an investigation into the 737 quality control system and imposed certain additional requirements and restrictions. As part of our plan to improve quality and safety and to address the issues identified, we slowed production rates and delayed planned production rate increases to reduce traveled work in our factory, as well as at our suppliers. We have also taken additional actions to improve safety and quality, including investing in workforce training, simplifying plans and processes, eliminating defects, and enhancing our safety and quality culture. The 737-9 door plug accident and our resulting actions, including slowing production, significantly impacted our financial position, results of operations and cash flows during 2024 and 2025. On November 4, 2024, the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers District 751 (IAM 751), representing approximately 30,000 Boeing employees, voted to ratify a new contract, thereby ending the work stoppage initiated on September 13, 2024, which paused production of certain commercial aircraft models (737, 767, 777 and 777X aircraft) as well as production of commercial derivative aircraft for our Defense, Space & Security business (KC-46A Tanker and P-8A Poseidon). Production for all programs resumed in December 2024 and gradually ramped up during 2025. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: An investment in our securities involves risks and uncertainties, including those described below, which can materially affect our business, financial position, results of operations and cash flows. These risk factors should be carefully reviewed in conjunction with the other information in this report, including “Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” and the Consolidated Financial Statements and related notes. Due to risks and uncertainties, known and unknown, our past financial results may not be a reliable indicator of future performance, and historical trends should not be used to anticipate results or trends in future periods. Risks Related to Our Business and Operations We depend heavily on commercial airlines, subjecting us to unique risks. Market conditions have a significant impact on demand for our commercial aircraft and related services. The commercial aircraft market is predominantly driven by long-term trends in airline passenger and cargo traffic. The principal factors underlying long-term traffic growth are sustained economic growth and political stability in both developed and emerging markets. Demand for our commercial aircraft is further influenced by additional factors including airline profitability, availability of aircraft financing, trade policies, geopolitics, technological advances, price and other competitive factors, fuel prices, inflationary pressures, terrorism, pandemics, epidemics, sustainability-related preferences, environmental regulations, and reputational factors. Historically, the airline industry has been cyclical and very competitive and has experienced significant profit swings and constant challenges to be more cost competitive. Significant deterioration in the global economic environment, the airline industry generally or the financial stability of one or more of our major customers could result in fewer new orders for aircraft or services, or could cause customers to seek to postpone or cancel contractual orders and/or payments to us, which could result in lower revenues, profitability and cash flows and a reduction in our contractual backlog. In addition, because our commercial aircraft backlog consists of aircraft scheduled for delivery over a period of several years, any of these macroeconomic, industry or customer impacts could affect deliveries over a long period. We enter into firm fixed-price aircraft sales contracts with indexed price escalation clauses, which subjects us to losses if we have cost overruns or if increases in our costs exceed the applicable escalation rate. Commercial aircraft sales contracts are typically entered into years before the aircraft are delivered. In order to help account for economic fluctuations between the contract date and delivery date, aircraft pricing generally consists of a fixed amount as modified by price escalation formulas derived from labor, commodity and other price indices. Our revenue estimates are based on current expectations with respect to these escalation formulas, but the actual escalation amounts are outside of our control. Escalation factors can fluctuate significantly from period to period.

credit_strengths.text: Boeing's revenue base is substantial and diversified across commercial aircraft, defense, space and services, with the latest fiscal year showing a sharp rebound from the prior year's trough. This scale supports the issuer's market position as one of two major manufacturers of large commercial jets and a top-tier defense contractor, providing a broad platform for cash generation as production normalizes.

Operating income returned to positive territory after two consecutive years of losses, and operating cash flow turned positive, indicating that the worst of the operational disruption from the door plug accident and labor stoppages is behind. The recovery in both metrics suggests improving execution and a path toward more stable internal cash generation.

key_risks.text: The risk factor passage highlights that Boeing depends heavily on commercial airlines and is exposed to cyclical demand, customer financial stability, and order deferrals. Because the commercial aircraft backlog spans several years, any macroeconomic or industry downturn could suppress deliveries and cash flows for an extended period, while fixed-price contracts with indexed escalation clauses leave Boeing exposed to cost overruns if actual escalation lags.

The debt note shows a significant maturity wall, with the next twelve months representing the largest single-year repayment obligation, followed by a smaller but still material year five. This concentration requires refinancing or substantial cash generation, yet free cash flow is negative and operating cash flow is modest relative to the debt load, creating refinancing risk if capital markets tighten or operational recovery stalls.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is thin at roughly one and a half times, well below the sector median, and free cash flow is negative, meaning the issuer currently relies on cash balances or external financing to meet obligations. With capital expenditures exceeding operating cash flow, internal funds do not cover investing needs, let alone debt service, leaving little margin for error.

Liquidity provides some cushion, with a current ratio slightly below the sector median and a cash balance that covers only a fraction of total debt. The maturity profile concentrates repayments in the near term, and with negative free cash flow, the issuer may need to refinance or draw on revolver capacity, making liquidity management critical over the next twelve months.

overall_credit_view.text: Boeing's credit profile is highly leveraged, with gross and net leverage multiples far above sector medians and an indicative financial risk profile that sits at the weaker end of the scale. The combination of high debt, weak cash flow conversion, and thin interest coverage places the issuer in a vulnerable position, though the recent revenue and operating income recovery offers some hope for deleveraging if sustained.

Our forward view is that credit quality hinges on whether Boeing can translate its backlog into consistent deliveries and positive free cash flow while managing the upcoming maturity wall. If operational execution improves and cash flow turns sustainably positive, leverage could trend lower; otherwise, refinancing risk and reliance on external funding will persist, keeping the credit under pressure.

credit_strengths.text: 波音的收益基礎龐大且多元化，涵蓋商用飛機、國防、太空及服務，最近一個財政年度顯示較前一年低谷大幅反彈。此規模支持發行人的市場地位，使其成為兩家大型商用噴射機製造商之一及頂級國防承包商，隨著生產正常化，提供廣闊的現金產生平台。
營業收入在連續兩年虧損後回復正數，營運現金流亦轉正，顯示門塞事故及勞工停工造成的最嚴重營運干擾已經過去。兩項指標的復甦顯示執行力改善，並朝向更穩定的內部現金產生邁進。

key_risks.text: 風險因素段落強調，波音高度依賴商用航空公司，並面臨週期性需求、客戶財務穩定性及訂單延遲的風險。由於商用飛機訂單積壓橫跨數年，任何宏觀經濟或行業低迷可能壓抑交付及現金流一段較長時間，而設有指數化遞增條款的固定價格合約，若實際遞增落後，將使波音面臨成本超支的風險。
債務附註顯示存在顯著的到期牆，未來十二個月代表最大的單一年度還款義務，其後第五年雖較小但仍屬重大。此集中度需要再融資或大量現金產生，然而自由現金流為負，且營運現金流相對於債務負擔而言僅屬溫和，若資本市場收緊或營運復甦停滯，將產生再融資風險。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率薄弱，約為一點五倍，遠低於行業中位數，且自由現金流為負，意味著發行人目前依賴現金結餘或外部融資來履行義務。由於資本支出超過營運現金流，內部資金不足以覆蓋投資需求，更遑論償還債務，容錯空間甚微。
流動性提供部分緩衝，流動比率略低於行業中位數，現金結餘僅覆蓋總債務的一小部分。到期結構將還款集中於近期，且自由現金流為負，發行人可能需要再融資或動用循環信貸額度，使流動性管理在未來十二個月至關重要。

overall_credit_view.text: 波音的信用狀況槓桿高企，總槓桿及淨槓桿倍數遠高於行業中位數，指示性財務風險狀況處於尺度的較弱一端。高債務、疲弱的現金流轉換及薄弱的利息覆蓋相結合，使發行人處於脆弱位置，儘管近期收益及營業收入復甦若持續，則為去槓桿帶來一些希望。
我們的前瞻觀點是，信用質素取決於波音能否將訂單積壓轉化為持續交付及正自由現金流，同時管理即將到期的債務牆。若營運執行改善且現金流持續轉正，槓桿可能趨降；否則，再融資風險及對外部資金的依賴將持續，使信用受壓。
